findings.F1: The Calmar that failed (0.37) is set by one fall: the book lost 26.4 % over 214 days from w1 to w3 while holding the coins lost 60.6 %, with book returns of −10.9 % in w2 and −10.3 % in w3 (holding −41.7 % and −21.4 %), and the signal trades summed to −1.42 and −1.10 in those two windows.
findings.F2: Inside that fall the losses came from Sunday falls in coins that had been rising: in w2–w3 the signal cases in the top third of the prior 20-day return (above +4.1 %) had an excess 3-day return of −5.0 % (t −3.2, 78 cases), while the bottom third (20-day return below −13 %) still rebounded +2.1 % (t 2.4, 78 cases).
findings.F3: Over all windows the rebound is carried entirely by coins already down over 20 days: excess 3-day return +1.99 % (t 5.4, 659 cases) in the bottom third of the 20-day return (below −10.6 %), +0.45 % (t 1.5) in the middle third, and 0.00 % (t 0.0) in the top third (above +5.3 %); the price against its 50-day mean shows the same pattern (bottom third +1.37 %, t 3.5; others +0.2 %).
findings.F4: The 20-day-fall condition is not an effect of its own: Sundays without the signal in the bottom third of the 20-day return had an excess 3-day return of −1.60 % (t −5.7, 688 cases), against +1.99 % when the weekend fall is present. The rebound belongs to the weekend fall itself and fits the theory: a thin weekend book is pushed furthest when one-sided selling is already under way.
findings.F5: Restricting the signal to a 20-day return below +5.3 % cut the approximate weekly book's deepest fall from −23.6 % to −9.5 % and raised its Calmar from 0.51 to 1.04, with Sharpe 0.96 against 0.85. The yearly return was nearly kept (9.9 % against 12.1 %), over 197 active weeks.
findings.F6: The idea's volatility weighting does not repair the falls: trading only when 20-day volatility is above its 60-day level gave Calmar 0.37 and a deepest fall of −12.4 %, but kept only a 4.6 % yearly return.
findings.F7: Volatility does help inside the falling coins: with a 20-day return in the bottom third, cases with 20-day volatility above its 60-day level had +3.14 % excess (t 5.85, 196 cases) against +0.36 % (t 0.57, 202 cases) below it. Volatility alone on no-signal Sundays earns −0.92 % (t −2.05) in its top third, so it is not an effect of its own.
findings.F8: The weakest cases lose: the smallest third of Sunday falls (above −1.3 %) had an excess of −0.56 % (t −2.1, 804 cases) and the lowest-forecast third −0.34 % (t −1.1). The largest third of falls (below −3.1 %) had +1.57 % (t 3.9) and the top forecast third +1.42 % (t 3.8).

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days (Monday to Wednesday), the larger the weekend fall the larger the rise, only while the coin's own 20-day return is negative, and the rise is larger the deeper that 20-day fall.
ideas.consequence: Buy weekend falls at Sunday's close and hold through Wednesday in coins already down over the past 20 days, and refuse the weekend falls of coins that have been rising, where the rebound fails and the book's deepest falls came from.
ideas.name: weekend fall rebound in downtrend

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days (Monday to Wednesday), the larger the weekend fall the larger the rise, only while the coin's 20-day return is negative, and the rise is larger the more its 20-day volatility of daily returns exceeds its 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: Among weekend falls of coins already falling, give the largest position to those whose recent volatility has risen above its longer level, and the smallest to quiet ones.
ideas.name: agitated downtrend weekend rebound
